analysis: Both changes are test-only edits in live MLX suites that are gated off by default (DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_TESTS=1 plus a model-specific flag). They add handling for a new `.toolCallDelta` stream event case so the switch statements remain exhaustive. GemmaToolCallLiveTests.swift line 265 records an Issue if a named tool_choice call is ever streamed as a delta, which asserts that forced-choice calls are not fragmented. Qwen36ProductionCanaryTests.swift lines 389-391 append only the completed call from a delta (`delta.completed`) and ignore partial fragments, so tool-call accumulation is unchanged. Neither file touches production code, provider keys, attestation, coordinator WebSocket handling, prefix-cache crypto, or authorization. No test fixture logs or exposes secrets; the Gemma test prints prompts built from synthetic data only. The Qwen test file is unchanged otherwise, and its base text was reviewed only to place the patch in context. For T-041 and the cache surface, the Qwen fixture sets DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 in test environments, so there is no new cache-at-rest exposure. The production source defining `.toolCallDelta` (the streaming-delta feature) is not in this batch, so its security properties, such as whether partial tool-call fragments are emitted post-encryption and whether the TB-002 encryption fail-closed behavior (T-008) is preserved, need review in the other PR units. No findings in this batch.
